analysis: Reviewed the head_text excerpt (lines 884-1016) of scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py. It is a CI workflow unit-test file with no runtime provider code. The visible part contains tests for sparse-checkout patterns (SPARSE_PATTERNS, which skip only evidence tarballs and landing media), composite-action build steps (asserting no cache-hit bypass, no --filter/--skip), cache key structure, and SwiftPM repository cache keying (runner layout, lane, Package.resolved hash). These are test-only assertions that tighten CI integrity expectations. Their implications for provider artifact integrity (A-011, T-034) are indirect and not weakened here. Test fixtures use temporary directories and local git, with no secrets or network access. I found no regression against T-041 or the other provider threats; the retained T-041 cache threat is not touched by this file. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and covers earlier changes (route job runs-on via fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes), matrix shards, Blacksmith runner selection). The actual workflow files, action.yml and route job are not supplied. Any security implications of the runner routing change, such as a Darkbloom macOS sandbox used for CI and cache save/restore trust across PR boundaries, cannot be evaluated from this unit. Integration should check those workflow files for cache poisoning via restore-keys and for untrusted PR code on privileged runners.
